tasks.title: Observational Test - Planetarium Part I: Question 1
tasks.statement: The sky projected in the dome corresponds to Suceava (Long 260 15’), at 18:00 UT, on a certain day of a certain month. Two arcs will then be projected. The arcs are segmented. Each segment represents an interval of some number of degrees. Note that this number is not the same for each arc.

parts.question: Identify each arc by circling the correct name and give the angular size of each segment (in degrees). First arc and Second arc (Equator, Meridian, Ecliptic) and segment sizes.
parts.reference: First arc length – length – MERIDIAN 10º - 1p+2p; Second arc segment length – EQUATOR 15º - 1p+2p

parts.question: Estimate the local sidereal time of the sky you see in the dome.
parts.reference: sidereal – 13h30m. +/- 15 m – full points; +/- 30 m half points

parts.question: Determine the month to which the projected sky would correspond at the given time. Fill in the box the number of the month (1 to 12).

tasks.title: Observational Test - Planetarium Part I: Question 2
tasks.statement: For questions 2 and 3 the assistant will use a small red arrow pointer to point some objects in the sky. Each object will be pointed at for 2 minutes (30 seconds arrow pointer on and 10 seconds off). Please pay attention to the assistant announcements.

parts.question: The locations of three Messier objects will be pointed at one by one. For each Messier object pointed to, fill in the boxes with its Messier catalog number and the number which indicates its type (1 for galaxy, 2 for nebula, 3 for open cluster, 4 for globular cluster). Also, for each object, fill in the IAU abbreviation of the constellation where the star is located.
parts.reference: 1st Messier object: M101, type 1 (2p), UMa (1p+2p); 2nd Messier object: M57, type 2 (2p), Lyr (1p+2p); 3rd Messier object: M92, type 4 (2p), Her (1p+2p)

tasks.title: Observational Test - Planetarium Part I: Question 3
tasks.statement: For questions 2 and 3 the assistant will use a small red arrow pointer to point some objects in the sky. Each object will be pointed at for 2 minutes (30 seconds arrow pointer on and 10 seconds off). Please pay attention to the assistant announcements.

parts.question: Three stars will be pointed at successively. Each star will be pointed at for 2 minutes. Fill the appropriate box with the name of the star (or the Bayer designation) and the number which indicates its type (1 for single, 2 double). For each star, also fill in the IAU abbreviation of the constellation where the star is located.
parts.reference: 1st Star:  UMi / Kochab, type 1 (2p), UMi (1p+2p); 2nd Star:  Leo / Algieba, type 2 (2p), Leo (1p+2p); 3rd Star:  CVn / Cor Caroli, type 2 (2p), CVn (1p+2p)

tasks.title: Observational Test - Planetarium Part II: Sky Chart Questions
tasks.statement: The map represents the sky in Suceava (Latitude 470 39’ North, Longitude 260 15’ East) at 19:00 UT on the day of test. The observer who made the sky-map was at a very high altitude above Suceava; the Zenith point is in the center of the chart. Solve question 1 to 4 on one copy of the map and questions 5 to 8 on the second copy of map.

parts.question: Draw on the map the horizon for an observer located on the ground in Suceava.
Draw the celestial equator, the ecliptic, the galactic equator and the local meridian on the map with continuous lines.

Mark the cardinal points (as N for north, E for east, S for south and W for west). Mark all the planets (except Uranus and Neptune) of the Solar System on the map and number them as 1, 2, …,6 in the order of increasing orbital radius (Skip number 3 for the Earth).
parts.reference: 0.5p for each cardinal point (0.5p x 4 = 2p); 1.4p for each planet (1.4p x 5 = 7p)

parts.question: Identify and mark the four brightest stars in visual band above the horizon line. Number the star starting from 1 – the brightest, and continue with the fainter ones till number 4 for the faintest. Fill in the table the Bayer name of the four identified stars.
parts.reference: each star name 0.5p + at correct position in the list 0.5p. 1:  Boo (Arcturus), 2:  Lyr (Vega), 3:  Aur (Capella), 4:  Aql (Altair)

parts.question: Draw approximate figures of any 15 constellations which lie completely above the horizon on the map. Each constellation you mark should be identified on the map with the IAU abbreviation.
Mark on the map the positions of the following objects: a. The Messier objects: M31, M27, M13; b.  Cygni,  Ursa Minoris.
Estimate the sidereal time of the map; write the value in the box to the right.
Estimate the equatorial coordinates (right ascension and declination) of the star Altair (α Aquilae). Write your answer in the box.
